hospitals.description: Children's Hospital of Richmond at VCU is the pediatric arm of VCU Health and the academic children's hospital for central Virginia, run inside the VCU Medical Center campus in downtown Richmond. Its 16-story Children's Tower, opened in April 2023, holds the pediatric inpatient floors, the children's emergency department and the region's only Level I pediatric trauma center. Neonatal care is a long-standing strength: the program opened the first NICU in Virginia in 1973 and now runs a Level IV unit that serves as a regional referral center, with a new 20-bed NICU moving into the Tower in early 2026. The campus sits just off I-95 near the Capitol and the Church Hill and Shockoe neighborhoods.
highlights: Level I pediatric trauma and burn center, the only one in central Virginia
Level IV NICU; 20-bed NICU opening in the Children's Tower in January 2026 alongside existing NICU beds in VCU Medical Center
Children's Tower opened April 30, 2023: 16 stories, about $420 million, 72 private acute and intensive care rooms
24 more acute care beds under construction on Tower Level 11, due late 2026
PICU holds an AACN Beacon Award (silver)
Magnet designation (2011, 2016, 2020 per Wikipedia)
Academic home of the VCU School of Medicine pediatrics program

hospitals.description: CHKD is the only freestanding children's hospital in Virginia, a 266-bed teaching hospital on the Eastern Virginia Medical School campus in Norfolk's Ghent area. It serves all of Hampton Roads and northeastern North Carolina, running a 32-bed PICU, a Level IV NICU and a pediatric emergency department that sees about 60,000 visits a year as the region's Level I pediatric trauma center. Since 2022 the campus has also included the 14-story Children's Pavilion with 60 private inpatient psychiatric rooms. A large network of CHKD primary care practices, health centers, urgent cares and surgery centers stretches from Williamsburg to Virginia Beach and Chesapeake.
highlights: Virginia's only freestanding children's hospital, 266 beds
32-bed PICU, the largest pediatric critical care unit in the region (about 1,500 admissions a year)
Level IV NICU with 60 private rooms plus 10 double rooms
Level I pediatric trauma center; ED sees about 60,000 visits a year
ACS-verified Level 1 Children's Surgery Center
Children's Pavilion mental health hospital (2022), 60 private inpatient rooms
Birthplace of the Nuss procedure for pectus excavatum; runs Virginia's only donor human milk bank

hospitals.description: UVA Health Children's is the pediatric hospital inside the University of Virginia's academic medical center in Charlottesville and the top-ranked children's hospital in Virginia by U.S. News. It runs a Level IV NICU billed as the region's most advanced, a 25-bed PICU with about 1,000 admissions a year that also serves as a referral center for pediatric heart patients, and pediatric emergency and trauma care on the main hospital campus. Patients come from across central Virginia, the Shenandoah Valley and Southside, and UVA also partners with CHKD in Norfolk. The hospital sits next to the UVA Grounds, a short walk from downtown Charlottesville and the Blue Ridge foothills.
highlights: Ranked No. 1 children's hospital in Virginia by U.S. News & World Report
Level IV NICU, the highest neonatal level
25-bed PICU (24 private rooms), about 1,000 admissions a year, pediatric cardiac referral center
Inside a Level I trauma center; University Medical Center has 679 beds and about 77,000 ED visits (FY2025)
Cancer care within Virginia's first NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center
Academic home of UVA School of Medicine pediatrics

hospitals.description: Carilion Children's is the pediatric program of Carilion Clinic, based inside Carilion Roanoke Memorial Hospital, the Level I trauma and teaching hospital for southwest Virginia. Its fact sheet lists a 24-bed inpatient unit, an 8-bed PICU that is the only one in the region, and a 60-bed Level IIIB NICU described as the largest in western Virginia. The hospital houses a dedicated pediatric emergency department and is western Virginia's only Level I pediatric trauma center, backed by a neonatal and pediatric transport team that brings in children from a wide rural catchment. Roanoke sits in the Blue Ridge with quick access to the Parkway, the Roanoke River greenways and Smith Mountain Lake.
highlights: Western Virginia's only Level I pediatric trauma center
8-bed PICU, the only PICU in the region
60-bed Level IIIB NICU, the region's largest
Dedicated pediatric emergency department at Carilion Roanoke Memorial
Neonatal and pediatric transport team
Pediatrics department includes 14 advanced care practitioners (2024 fact sheet)
Teaching site for Virginia Tech Carilion School of Medicine
hospitals.notes: Main pediatric acute care employer in western Virginia. peds_beds 92 is the sum of the fact sheet's 24 inpatient, 8 PICU and 60 NICU beds. beds is the Wikipedia infobox figure for Carilion Roanoke Memorial (703; the article text says 825). NICU recorded as level 3 (fact sheet says Level IIIB). Carilion Roanoke Memorial has Magnet status per the Wikipedia hospital list note, but that note is for Roanoke Community and Memorial together, so magnet left null.

hospitals.description: Bon Secours St. Mary's is the flagship Bon Secours hospital in Richmond, a 391-bed Catholic hospital in the near West End off Bremo Road. It runs the Bon Secours pediatric program for the Richmond market, including a 24-hour pediatric emergency department and a Level III NICU that a national neonatal directory lists at 21 beds, plus a group of hospital-based pediatric subspecialists in surgery, endocrinology and neurology. It is the main private-system alternative to VCU's children's hospital for families in Henrico, Goochland and the western suburbs. The campus sits between the Libbie and Grove shopping district and the I-64 corridor.
highlights: 391-bed Bon Secours flagship in Richmond's West End
Dedicated 24-hour pediatric emergency department
Level III NICU (21 beds per neonatologysolutions directory)
Hospital-based pediatric surgery, endocrinology and neurology practices actively recruiting
Bon Secours publishes a Richmond pediatric impact report for its children's services

hospitals.description: Chippenham Hospital is the south Richmond campus of HCA's CJW Medical Center, a combined 667-bed license with Johnston-Willis that Wikipedia lists as a Level I trauma center. Chippenham runs a dedicated children's emergency room, which HCA promotes as a separate kids' ER, and HCA concentrated its Richmond pediatric inpatient care here after closing the pediatric units at Henrico Doctors' Hospital in 2022. Its NICU was folded into the Johnston-Willis NICU in August 2022, so newborn intensive care for CJW now sits on the Midlothian Turnpike campus. The hospital is off Jahnke Road near the Chippenham Parkway, serving Chesterfield County and the city's Southside.
highlights: Dedicated pediatric emergency room (HCA Virginia kids' ER)
HCA's Richmond pediatric inpatient hub after Henrico Doctors' pediatric units closed in 2022 (verify)
Part of CJW Medical Center, a Level I trauma center (adult) with 667 beds across two campuses
NICU consolidated into Johnston-Willis in August 2022

hospitals.description: Johnston-Willis is the Midlothian Turnpike campus of HCA's CJW Medical Center in Chesterfield County, a busy obstetric hospital that became CJW's single NICU site when Chippenham's NICU merged into it in August 2022. A national neonatal directory lists the Johnston-Willis NICU as Level III with about 20 beds, and HCA lists NICU and labor and delivery as core services here. There is no separate pediatric inpatient unit or pediatric ER on this campus; children go to the Chippenham kids' ER a few miles east. The hospital sits in the fast-growing western Chesterfield suburbs near Bon Air and Midlothian.
highlights: CJW Medical Center's NICU site since the August 2022 consolidation
Level III NICU (about 20 beds per neonatologysolutions directory, before consolidation)
High-volume birthing center in western Chesterfield County
Shares the CJW license and Level I trauma designation with Chippenham
